title: SRE SLOs, Error Budgets, Capacity Planning, and Runbook Standards
author: Priya Nair
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document codifies Redwood Inference's standards for SLO definition and ownership, error budget policy, capacity planning methodology, incident review expectations, operational tooling, and runbook structure. It applies to all customer-facing inference services (hosted API, dedicated pools, private control plane) and the core serving runtime components.

Audience: SRE, Platform, Serving Runtime, and Product engineering teams.

1) SLOs and Error Budgets

Summary: SLOs are the primary operational contract between product owners and SRE. Each service must have at least one Availability SLO and one Latency SLO where applicable. Error budgets are computed monthly and govern release and traffic policy.

Required SLO metadata (per service):
- service_name: short, dash-separated (e.g., inference-gateway)
- owner: team or product owner (email + pager team)
- slo_type: availability | latency | correctness | throughput
- slo_definition: human readable and measurement expression
- slo_window: rolling 30-day (default) or specified (7 / 90)
- alerting_thresholds: burn-rate alerts and slo-violation alerts
- error_budget_policy: gating rules for deploys, feature flags, and rollouts

Example SLOs (recommended defaults):
| service | SLO (availability) | measurement | window | error budget |
| inference-gateway | 99.95% successful requests | 5xx + client-timeout / total requests | 30d | 21.6 minutes downtime/month |
| runtime-pool | 99.9% of model-ready requests | request-ready / total requests | 30d | 43.2 minutes/month |
| emb-embedder | p99 latency < 100ms | p99 of embedding requests | 30d | N/A (latency SLO) |

Error budget policy (standard):
1. Error budget computed as (1 - availability) * window. Track burn using hourly burn-rate windows (1h, 6h, 24h).
2. Burn-rate alert tiers:
   - Tier 1 (1h burn-rate > 2x): notify SRE slack channel, create a P1 if service degradation affects customers.
   - Tier 2 (6h burn-rate > 1.5x): pause non-critical releases for the service for 48 hours.
   - Tier 3 (24h burn-rate > 1.2x) OR budget exhausted: immediate freeze on feature rollouts + mandatory incident review within 48 hours.
3. Releases during an active burn must be accompanied by a rollback plan and explicit approval from the SRE on-call.
4. Self-service opt-outs (e.g., performance experiments) require documented waivers and acceptance criteria and must be tracked in the service's SLO page.

2) Capacity Planning and Autoscaling Standards

Objective: Maintain enough capacity to meet SLOs at the 95th percentile of expected load while minimizing cost. Capacity plans are required quarterly for all production services and reviewed at the SRE quarterly review.

Inputs and telemetry:
- historical traffic (7/30/90d p50/p90/p99)
- per-request GPU/CPU/Memory cost profile (sampled from runtime metrics)
- cold-start and model-load times
- multi-tenant interference signals (queue lengths, OOMs)
- planned product events (marketing, new customer onboarding)

Planning steps (quarterly):
1. Define target headroom: default 25% headroom at p95 expected load. Increase to 40% for month-of major launches.
2. Model resource utilization: compute tokens/sec and memory per concurrent session for representative workloads.
3. Convert to capacity units: define capacity unit = 1 GPU slot at standard model profile (e.g., A40-like). Compute required slots = ceil((p95_tokens_per_sec * avg_cost_per_token) / slot_throughput).
4. Validate with load tests: run 75/90/120 minute soak tests at p95 and p99 load with graceful degradation checks.
5. Document scaling policy: autoscale thresholds (CPU/GPU utilization, queue length, latency) and cooldown windows.

Autoscaling recommended thresholds (examples):
- Add replica when p95 latency > 80% of latency SLO AND queue length > 100 for 3 consecutive minutes.
- Remove replica when p95 latency < 50% of latency SLO AND CPU/GPU utilization < 40% for 10 minutes.
- Max scale step: double current replicas, min 1 replica.

Capacity runbook checklist (per release):
- Update capacity plan with expected traffic change (delta %)
- Run pre-release traffic simulation in staging or a canary pool
- Ensure autoscaler cooldowns are tuned to avoid oscillation
- Notify SRE and operations channels 48 hours before large traffic experiments

3) Reliability Initiatives and Program Structure

Goal: Structure continuous reliability work as measurable initiatives with owners, timelines, and KPIs. Examples: reducing cold-start rate by 50%, improving p99 tail latency by 30%, or cutting mean time to recovery (MTTR) by 20%.

Initiative template:
- title
- owner (name + team)
- target metric and baseline
- acceptance criteria
- major milestones and dates
- risks and mitigation
- post-mortem plan and rollout strategy

Quarterly cadence:
- Planning: define 3x top initiatives at the start of the quarter
- Mid-quarter review: show progress against milestones and metrics
- Completion: produce a short results doc and operationalize changes (dashboards, alerts, runbooks)

4) Incident Review Standards and Postmortem Expectations

When to produce a postmortem:
- All SEV1 and SEV2 incidents impacting customers or creating SLO burn beyond thresholds.
- Any incident that results in a regulatory or compliance exposure.

Postmortem structure (required):
1. Summary (one-paragraph)
2. Timeline (timestamped events)
3. Impact (customer-visible metrics, % requests affected)
4. Root cause analysis (5 whys + contributing factors)
5. Detection and mitigation timeline (what changed during the incident)
6. Corrective actions (short-term and long-term), owners, and target dates
7. Follow-up verification plan (how changes will be validated)
8. Lessons learned (actionable, not opinion)

Postmortem SLA: publish within 3 business days for SEV1, 7 business days for SEV2. Affected product and SRE leads must review and sign off.

Blamelessness: language in all postmortems must be blameless and focus on system/process fixes. Use objective measurements.

5) Operational Tooling and Observability Stack

Core telemetry and tooling (standard stack):
- Metrics: Prometheus + Thanos for long-term retention
- Dashboards: Grafana (per-service dashboards pre-populated by template)
- Tracing: Jaeger / Tempo for distributed trace collection
- Logs: Loki + structured request logs ingested into BigQuery for ad hoc queries
- Alerting: Alertmanager routed to PagerDuty + Slack channels (sre-alerts, product-alerts)
- Incident comms: Statuspage + internal incident channel template
- CI / Canary tooling: Argo Rollouts / Spinnaker for progressive delivery

Requirements and templates:
- Every production service must import the standard SRE Grafana dashboard template and populate variables (service_name, environment).
- Tracing must include a top-level span for request_id and model_hash.
- Structured logs must include: request_id, customer_id (or hashed_customer_id), model_name, model_version, latency_ms, response_size, error_code.

Alert hygiene:
- Alert noise budget: no more than 10 actionable alerts per oncall per week. Review noisy alerts quarterly and reduce by increasing thresholds or adding filters.
- Every alert must map to a runbook with explicit mitigation steps and ownership.

6) Runbook Standards and Templates

Purpose: Runbooks are the primary operational playbook for responders. They must be concise, prescriptive, and actionable. Each runbook must be reviewed at least once per quarter.

Runbook template (required headings):
- Title: service-name - incident type (e.g., inference-gateway - high 5xx rate)
- Pager escalation: primary oncall, secondary, escalation policy
- Detection: the alert name and Grafana dashboard links
- Impact assessment: how to quantify customer impact quickly (CLI commands / queries)
- Immediate mitigation steps (numbered)
- Diagnostics (commands, logs/queries, traces to check)
- Rollback and release controls (how to throttle or rollback)
- Post-incident checklist (tagging, SLA updates, postmortem owner)

Example excerpt (inference-gateway - high 5xx rate):
1. Pager fires: "inference-gateway-5xx-rate-high"
2. Assess scope: run query: SELECT count(*) FROM requests WHERE status >= 500 AND timestamp > now() - 15m GROUP BY model_name;
3. Mitigate: a) Scale up runtime-pool by +2 replicas for high priority customers. b) Apply temporary traffic-shed rule for non-paying tiers. c) If caused by a recent deploy, run: argo rollback inference-gateway --to-revision <previous>
4. Diagnostics: check 95th percentile latency for the last 30m, inspect traces for root span names "model_load" and "kv-cache-miss".

Runbook review checklist (quarterly):
- Owner verifies commands still work in staging
- Links to dashboards and queries are up-to-date
- Runbook tested during at least one game day per year

7) Oncall and Escalation Practices

Rotation: weekly primary oncall, monthly secondary oncall. Handoff notes required on rotation day.

Escalation policy: primary -> 10 minutes -> secondary -> 20 minutes -> SRE lead -> 30 minutes -> ENG execs if SEV1 continues.

Oncall playbook:
- Triage alerts within 5 minutes, acknowledge in PagerDuty, and post an incident channel stub with a short summary and incident owner.
- If recovering within 30 minutes and under error budget threshold, resolve with a short incident note and a 48-hour follow-up check.
- If not recovered within 30 minutes or budget risk exceeded, label as SEV and follow incident process (see related page).

8) Governance and Compliance

Documentation: every service SLO, runbook, and capacity plan must live in Confluence and reference the authoritative dashboards. SRE leadership audits SLO and runbook coverage monthly and publishes a remediation plan for gaps.

Exceptions: documented exceptions (waivers) to SLOs or policies must include a risk assessment, owner, and expiry date.

9) Appendix: Useful Commands and Queries

- Check error budget burn: SELECT service, SUM(errors)/SUM(total) as error_rate FROM telemetry.requests WHERE timestamp > now() - interval '30 days' GROUP BY service;
- Quick scale (kubectl example): kubectl scale deployment/runtime-pool -n prod --replicas=8
- Rollback Argo: argo rollouts undo inference-gateway -n prod --to-revision=<rev>
